content: 1. Serotonin modulators may enhance dopamine blockade, potentially increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome. 2. Antipsychotics may amplify the serotonergic effects of serotonin modulators, which could lead to serotonin syndrome. 3. Monitor patients for signs of serotonin toxicity, such as changes in mental status, autonomic instability, and neuromuscular hyperactivity, or for symptoms of neuroleptic malignant syndrome, including hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, and autonomic dysfunction. 4. Flurazepam and flibanserin both increase sedation; monitor closely. 5. The risk of sedation is heightened when flibanserin is co-administered with other central nervous system (CNS) depressants; modify therapy or monitor closely. 6. Fluvastatin increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism; monitor closely. 7. Co-administration of flibanserin with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase adverse effects; use caution and monitor closely. 8. Fluvoxamine increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism; modify therapy or monitor closely. 9. Co-administration of flibanserin with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors may increase flibanserin exposure, raising the risk of hypotension, syncope, and CNS depression; monitor closely. 10. Fosamprenavir increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 11. Co-administration of flibanserin with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 12. Fosphenytoin decreases the level or effect of flibanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 13. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce systemic exposure to flibanserin; monitor closely. 14. Flibanserin and ganaxolone both increase sedation; use caution and monitor closely. 15. Gemfibrozil increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism; modify therapy or monitor closely. 16. Ginkgo biloba increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 17. Grapefruit increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 18. Haloperidol increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Hydralazine increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 20. Hydrocodone and flibanserin both increase sedation; use caution and monitor closely. 21. Co-administration of drugs affecting the serotonergic neurotransmitter system may result in serotonin syndrome; monitor patients closely, especially during treatment initiation and dose adjustments. 22. Hydromorphone and flibanserin both increase sedation; modify therapy or monitor closely. 23. Hydroxyzine and flibanserin both increase sedation; modify therapy or monitor closely. 24. Idelalisib increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Ifosfamide increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 26. Iloperidone increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Imatinib increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Indinavir increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Irbesartan increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 30. Isoniazid increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Isoniazid also increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism; modify therapy or monitor closely. 32. Isradipine increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 33. Istradefylline increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 34. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials; consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 35. Itraconazole increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Ivosidenib decreases the level or effect of flibanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism; avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Ketoconazole increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 38. Lansoprazole increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 39. Lapatinib increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 40. Larotrectinib increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 41. Lasmiditan and flibanserin both increase sedation; use caution and monitor closely. 42. Co-administration of lasmiditan with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, has not been evaluated in clinical studies. Lasmiditan may cause sedation and other cognitive or neuropsychiatric adverse reactions. 43. Lemborexant and flibanserin both increase sedation; modify therapy or monitor closely. 44. Dosage adjustment may be necessary if lemborexant is co-administered with other CNS depressants due to potentially additive effects. 45. Lenacapavir increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 46. Lenvatinib increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 47. Levetiracetam and flibanserin both increase sedation; use caution and monitor closely. 48. Levocetirizine and flibanserin both increase sedation; use caution and monitor closely. 49. Levoketoconazole increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 50. Levorphanol and flibanserin both increase sedation; modify therapy or monitor closely. 51. Lidocaine increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 52. Lomustine increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 53. Lonafarnib increases the AUC and peak concentration of CYP2C19 substrates; avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the CYP2C19 substrate dose as per product labeling. 54. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; co-administration is contraindicated. 55. Loratadine and flibanserin both increase sedation; use caution and monitor closely. 56. Lorazepam and flibanserin both increase sedation; modify therapy or monitor closely. 57. Lorlatinib decreases the level or effect of flibanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism; avoid or use alternative drugs. 58. Losartan increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 59. Lovastatin increases the level or effect of flibanserin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely. 60. Flibanserin and loxapine both affect CYP3A4 metabolism; use caution and monitor closely.
